cards.text: This song is by David, Israel's king, who kept his father's sheep when he was young (1 Samuel 16:11). He opens with one line that sets up the whole song: "The LORD is my shepherd". Friend, a sheep with THAT shepherd is SET.

cards.question: Because the LORD is his shepherd, David says he will never ___ anything he needs.

cards.text: The LORD makes David lie down in green pastures and leads him beside quiet waters. My best nap in that junk drawer was on a pile of old takeout menus, and friend, that was NOT green pastures.

cards.question: Green pastures and quiet waters. What's the feel of this picture David paints?

cards.text: Out in a pasture like that, a worn-out sheep gets its strength back. Then David's next line turns to his own soul.

cards.question: On the inside, David says the LORD does this for his soul: He ___ it.
Next, the LORD guides David in the paths of righteousness. David says the LORD does it because David earned it.

cards.text: Then the road turns, and David sings, "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death". It's like that dark back road where you turn the radio DOWN so you can see better.

cards.question: Even in the valley of the shadow of death, David says he will fear no evil. Why?

answers.text: Because the LORD is with him

cards.question: Up to the valley, David talks about the LORD: He makes me lie down, He leads me. In the valley, he sings, "for You are with me". So now David is talking right to the LORD.

cards.text: Out in that dark valley, David thinks about the shepherd's rod and staff. Now, a big stick in a scary place could go either way, right?

cards.question: In the valley of the shadow of death, what does David say the LORD's rod and staff do for him?

cards.text: Then the picture flips. No more sheep in a field: David's a guest now, and the LORD is the host.

cards.question: Like a host welcoming a guest, the LORD prepares a ___ for David.
David says the LORD prepares his table far away from his enemies.

cards.text: Then the LORD anoints David's head with oil. Friend, the last thing anybody poured on MY head was drawer dust.

cards.question: At the LORD's table, David says his cup overflows. What is that picture saying?

cards.text: Last line, and David looks ahead at the rest of his life. No five-year plan here, friend: this one covers ALL the days.

cards.question: With a shepherd and host like the LORD, what does David say will follow him all the days of his life?
To close his song, where does David say he will dwell forever?

answers.text: In the house of the LORD

findings.problem: The setup line 'a worn-out sheep gets its strength back' is a plain synonym of 'restores', the answer to card 6. It gives the answer away and rules out the wrong answers 'tests' and 'weighs' before the baker reasons anything out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Psalm 23:3 gives the reason the LORD guides David: 'for the sake of His name.' No story card tells it. Card 7 only asks the baker to reject a reason ('because David earned it'), so the baker can finish Prep without ever hearing the real reason, which is an important detail of the verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'With a shepherd and host like the LORD,' which rules out both negative wrong answers ('Trouble and sorrow', 'Hunger and thirst'). This is especially clear after 'I shall not want' and 'my cup overflows'. The right answer is the only one that fits the tone, so the card is a giveaway, not a choice.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
